components.label: Push coordinator

components.label: GPU batch queue
components.responsibility: Admit into a finite queue by chunk identity; reject when full and never treat rejection as completed work.

components.label: Synthetic batch worker

components.label: Subscriber ACK slots

components.label: Coalescing CDN fill

components.label: Session ACK reducer
components.responsibility: Verify subscriber, session epoch and outstanding chunk ID; delete once. Unknown or duplicate ACKs change no occupancy.

components.label: Slow-session policy
components.responsibility: Expire or disconnect a session under declared deadline, release its local slots and retain explicit undelivered IDs; do not count them as acknowledged.

components.label: Conservation ledger
components.responsibility: For every submitted chunk and subscriber record delivered/ACKed/rejected/unfinished outcome; separate compute totals from fan-out totals.

components.label: Chunk producer
components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Manifest publisher
components.responsibility: Compute finite immutable chunks once, publish a committed manifest, and let each subscriber pull at its own rate through the CDN.

components.label: Bounded batch admission
components.responsibility: Admit source chunks into a finite deduplicated batch queue independent of subscriber demand; expose rejected identities.

components.label: GPU chunk writer
components.responsibility: Finish modeled batch output, hash bytes and store immutable chunk before publishing its manifest entry.

components.label: Immutable chunk spool
components.responsibility: Store immutable content keys with explicit retained sequence floor and per-stream byte budget; pruning never silently rewrites an old key.

components.label: Versioned manifest
components.responsibility: Publish sorted committed chunk identities and explicit gaps/rejections in an immutable version; consumer advances only past declared outcomes.

components.label: Subscriber pull cursor
components.responsibility: Subscriber requests next identity with bounded concurrency and advances after its own successful receipt; publisher has no per-chunk push wait.

components.label: Coalesced CDN reader
components.responsibility: Coalesce identical content-key misses; cap distinct fills and waiters, verify payload hash, and keep fill cancellation independent per waiter.

components.label: Retention reset
components.responsibility: Return 410 with current floor and manifest version; require an explicit skip/reset or archived recovery source rather than claiming continuous delivery.

requirements.text: Bound GPU batch queue, fan-out slots and cache-fill work; retain explicit rejected and unfinished chunks.
Acknowledge per-subscriber delivery separately from compute completion; a slow subscriber cannot silently consume unbounded memory.
Coalesce concurrent same-chunk CDN misses; define cancellation, retry identity and retained-history expiry.

problem.scope: Authored bounded streaming study retaining the catalogue scope: synthetic finite video chunks, GPU batch work, acknowledged fan-out slots, coalescing CDN cache and one slow consumer. Compare push fan-out with bounded rejection against pull delivery from immutable CDN chunks. No codec, player, real GPU speedup, production sizing or infinite-stream claim.

acceptanceCases.then: One fill executes, live waiter receives matching bytes, canceled waiter receives no completion, and failures release in-flight entries.

guarantees: Per-session occupancy is bounded; ACK and compute completion are not conflated.

solutions.chooseWhen: Low delivery latency matters and slow consumers may be rejected or disconnected under explicit policy.

stages.explanation: Admit finite chunk work, execute bounded GPU batches and retain separate per-subscriber outstanding identities until acknowledged. GPU completion and each subscriber ACK are separate states. [Presence information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presence_information) describes a recently observed connection or activity. It is time-bounded evidence, not proof that a person or device will remain reachable after the observation.
invariants: GPU completion and each subscriber ACK are separate states.
stages.question: Does computed mean delivered?
stages.reason: Admit finite chunk work, execute bounded GPU batches and retain separate per-subscriber outstanding identities until acknowledged.
stages.title: Expose Push coordinator

stages.explanation: Admit into a finite queue by chunk identity; reject when full and never treat rejection as completed work. Every submitted chunk is queued, rejected or explicitly unfinished. [A queue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queue_%28abstract_data_type%29) separates accepting work from completing it. Capacity, ordering, ownership, and shutdown behavior determine what producers and consumers may safely assume about each item.
invariants: Every submitted chunk is queued, rejected or explicitly unfinished.
stages.question: What if production outruns GPU batch completion?
stages.reason: Admit into a finite queue by chunk identity; reject when full and never treat rejection as completed work.
stages.title: Bound pending compute

stages.explanation: Claim a batch with stable chunk IDs; record modeled compute completion before fan-out. Batching speed is a parameter, not measured hardware proof. A duplicate chunk identity cannot change immutable output bytes. [Data ingestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_integration) moves source records into a usable destination. Stable source identity and progress records distinguish genuinely new data from repeated delivery or a restarted import.
invariants: A duplicate chunk identity cannot change immutable output bytes.
stages.question: Can one timed-out request duplicate compute identity?
stages.reason: Claim a batch with stable chunk IDs; record modeled compute completion before fan-out. Batching speed is a parameter, not measured hardware proof.
stages.title: Complete one finite batch

stages.explanation: Track outstanding chunk IDs per subscriber/session with a fixed window; full subscribers receive a visible refusal or disconnection. No subscriber holds more than its configured window. [Stream processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream_processing) updates results as events arrive. Arrival order may differ from event time, so late-data rules and bounded retained state are part of the result definition.
invariants: No subscriber holds more than its configured window.
stages.question: Why should one slow subscriber not block all recipients?
stages.reason: Track outstanding chunk IDs per subscriber/session with a fixed window; full subscribers receive a visible refusal or disconnection.
stages.title: Allocate independent windows

stages.explanation: Maintain immutable content-key cache and single in-flight promise per key; bound distinct fill concurrency and waiter count. A fill failure clears the in-flight entry so a later explicit retry may proceed. [A cache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache_replacement_policies) keeps reusable results in limited memory. Eviction controls space, while ownership and invalidation rules determine whether a returned value is still safe to use.
invariants: A fill failure clears the in-flight entry so a later explicit retry may proceed.
stages.question: Can simultaneous subscribers trigger duplicate origin work?
stages.reason: Maintain immutable content-key cache and single in-flight promise per key; bound distinct fill concurrency and waiter count.
stages.title: Share a cache miss

stages.explanation: Verify subscriber, session epoch and outstanding chunk ID; delete once. Unknown or duplicate ACKs change no occupancy. An old session cannot free a new-session outstanding chunk. [Idempotence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence) means repeating the same logical operation does not repeat its effect. Stable request identities let a retry recover an existing outcome instead of creating another change.
invariants: An old session cannot free a new-session outstanding chunk.
stages.question: What if old ACKs arrive after reconnect?
stages.reason: Verify subscriber, session epoch and outstanding chunk ID; delete once. Unknown or duplicate ACKs change no occupancy.
stages.title: Release only a matching slot

stages.explanation: Expire or disconnect a session under declared deadline, release its local slots and retain explicit undelivered IDs; do not count them as acknowledged. Resource reclamation is not delivery success. [Time to live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_to_live) defines when a value or right stops being valid. Expiration must be checked at the point of use, even when background cleanup runs later.
invariants: Resource reclamation is not delivery success.
stages.question: What if ACK never arrives?
stages.reason: Expire or disconnect a session under declared deadline, release its local slots and retain explicit undelivered IDs; do not count them as acknowledged.
stages.title: Terminate held resources

stages.explanation: For every submitted chunk and subscriber record delivered/ACKed/rejected/unfinished outcome; separate compute totals from fan-out totals. The finite input ledger balances without inventing completion. [Publish–subscribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publish%E2%80%93subscribe_pattern) separates producing an update from distributing it to interested consumers. Delivery cost shifts depending on whether work is performed when writing or when someone reads. Consider this case: Two consumers, capacity one per subscriber, one ACK withheld.
invariants: The finite input ledger balances without inventing completion.
stages.question: Can rejected chunks disappear from the result?
stages.reason: For every submitted chunk and subscriber record delivered/ACKed/rejected/unfinished outcome; separate compute totals from fan-out totals.
stages.title: Reconcile finite outcomes

solutions.title: Bounded push fan-out with per-subscriber ACK windows
tradeoffs: Per-subscriber outstanding state grows with subscriber count times configured window.
Reject/drop policy must be visible; a slow subscriber cannot be promised lossless infinite retention.

stages.explanation: Compute finite immutable chunks once, publish a committed manifest, and let each subscriber pull at its own rate through the CDN. Each subscriber requests the next chunk only when it is ready. [A content delivery network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_network) serves reusable content near viewers. Cache keys, freshness rules, and origin fallback determine whether that improves latency without serving the wrong version.
invariants: Each subscriber requests the next chunk only when it is ready.
stages.question: Who decides when the slow consumer receives the next chunk?
stages.reason: Compute finite immutable chunks once, publish a committed manifest, and let each subscriber pull at its own rate through the CDN.

stages.explanation: Admit source chunks into a finite deduplicated batch queue independent of subscriber demand; expose rejected identities. Repeated pulls cannot schedule duplicate chunk computation. [Idempotence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence) means repeating the same logical operation does not repeat its effect. Stable request identities let a retry recover an existing outcome instead of creating another change.
invariants: Repeated pulls cannot schedule duplicate chunk computation.
stages.question: Can pull traffic create unlimited GPU work?
stages.reason: Admit source chunks into a finite deduplicated batch queue independent of subscriber demand; expose rejected identities.
stages.title: Admit finite compute work

stages.explanation: Finish modeled batch output, hash bytes and store immutable chunk before publishing its manifest entry. No advertised entry points to an uncommitted output. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version. Consider this case: Two consumers, capacity one per subscriber, one ACK withheld.
invariants: No advertised entry points to an uncommitted output.
stages.question: When may a manifest advertise a chunk?
stages.reason: Finish modeled batch output, hash bytes and store immutable chunk before publishing its manifest entry.
stages.title: Write immutable outputs

stages.explanation: Store immutable content keys with explicit retained sequence floor and per-stream byte budget; pruning never silently rewrites an old key. A pruned chunk returns expired, never a different chunk under the same identity. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version.
invariants: A pruned chunk returns expired, never a different chunk under the same identity.
stages.question: What if a subscriber pauses?
stages.reason: Store immutable content keys with explicit retained sequence floor and per-stream byte budget; pruning never silently rewrites an old key.
stages.title: Retain a finite replay window

stages.explanation: Publish sorted committed chunk identities and explicit gaps/rejections in an immutable version; consumer advances only past declared outcomes. A higher manifest version never changes old content hashes. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.
invariants: A higher manifest version never changes old content hashes.
stages.question: Can a subscriber skip a failed chunk?
stages.reason: Publish sorted committed chunk identities and explicit gaps/rejections in an immutable version; consumer advances only past declared outcomes.
stages.title: Publish committed sequence

stages.explanation: Subscriber requests next identity with bounded concurrency and advances after its own successful receipt; publisher has no per-chunk push wait. One slow cursor does not allocate publisher-side unbounded buffered chunks. [Presence information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presence_information) describes a recently observed connection or activity. It is time-bounded evidence, not proof that a person or device will remain reachable after the observation.
invariants: One slow cursor does not allocate publisher-side unbounded buffered chunks.
stages.question: Does the publisher hold an ACK slot while a subscriber sleeps?
stages.reason: Subscriber requests next identity with bounded concurrency and advances after its own successful receipt; publisher has no per-chunk push wait.
stages.title: Decouple slow demand

stages.explanation: Coalesce identical content-key misses; cap distinct fills and waiters, verify payload hash, and keep fill cancellation independent per waiter. Canceling one waiter does not cancel a fill still needed by others. [A condition variable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condition_variable) lets a thread sleep until shared state may have changed. Waking does not guarantee success, so the protected condition must be checked again.
invariants: Canceling one waiter does not cancel a fill still needed by others.
stages.question: What if many cursors miss one chunk?
stages.reason: Coalesce identical content-key misses; cap distinct fills and waiters, verify payload hash, and keep fill cancellation independent per waiter.

Retention loss remains a visible gap in finite-stream accounting. [A content delivery network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_network) serves reusable content near viewers. Cache keys, freshness rules, and origin fallback determine whether that improves latency without serving the wrong version.
invariants: Retention loss remains a visible gap in finite-stream accounting.

stages.reason: Return 410 with current floor and manifest version; require an explicit skip/reset or archived recovery source rather than claiming continuous delivery.
